transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Claire Zhang (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Tess Monroe (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (HavenMesh Partnerships), Owen Beckett (HavenMesh CTO), Lena Ortiz (HavenMesh Platform), Samir Patel (HavenMesh Security)
Shared: partner deck (link), preliminary routing diagram (link), SOC2 snapshot (link)

Summary: quick partner intro + compatibility framing call. Primary goals: understand HavenMesh reseller model + technical constraints, mapping of Redwood routing/fallbacks to HavenMesh marketplace, security and VPC constraints for Private/Dedicated options, and next steps to pilot routing and benchmark latency/cost.

00:00 Claire: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, i'm claire from Redwood inference, ae on partner go-to-market. we'll keep this tight 45ish mins, want to make sure we capture the technical constraints and a sample pilot plan.
00:14 Priya: thanks claire, excited to explore. we're havemesh, we resell curated GPU capacity to mid-market SaaS customers, want to see how Redwood can plug into our routing/orchestration so we can offer hosted + on-prem variants.
00:28 Marco: awesome, marco from redwood se. quick sanity question up front — are you expecting a direct API integration (we call it hosted pass-through) or running our private control plane in your VPCs? or both?
00:42 Owen: good q. our immediate ask is hosted pass-through for speed to market, but long term we'd like a private control plane option for enterprise customers. so we need both flavors supported in the integration.
00:56 Lena: and for a lot of our customers latency is a big deal — edge locations matter. we have regional POPs and sometimes on-prem nodes, so routing flexibility is key.
01:10 Claire: got it. that aligns with our typical partner integration patterns — we support three deployment modes: hosted API, dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools), and private (VPC/on-prem). you can route by policy: latency, cost, or region. we probably should walk through a couple of routing examples for your marketplace.
01:29 Priya: yes please — and also curious about commercial flow: how do we represent dedicated capacity SKUs in our catalog and what are the minimum commitments? but maybe we leave pricing to the end.
01:41 Marco: cool. i'll keep pricing light. technical first. one thing to flag: our runtime has automatic KV-caching and prefix caching, which matters for dialog flows. sometimes the transcript says K V cash which is funny — but basically we can cache token prefixes at the routing layer to reduce cost.
01:59 Samir: question on the private deployment side — our enterprise customers require SSO via SAML, KMS integration for key separation, and audit logs. do you have SOC2 or other certifications?
02:12 Claire: yes, we are SOC2 compliant and we have integrations with customer KMS providers; we can run the private control plane in your VPC and support HSM/KMS workflows. we'll share the SOC2 snapshot and an architecture diagram after this call.
02:28 Owen: great. also: on the hosted route, how does fall back look if a region is saturated — do you failover to other regions or to smaller quantized model variants? what's the latency implication?
02:42 Marco: two knobs — routing by region with cross-region failover, and model variant fallbacks (e.g., 8-bit quantized or smaller model family). failover adds RTT and possibly model switch costs; typical additional tail latency 30 to 200ms depending on distance and model size. we can present a chart later.
03:03 Lena: for our customers we need clear SLOs. what latency SLOs are typical for your dedicated pools?
03:13 Marco: dedicated pools aim for p95 generation latency targets under specific sequence lengths. e.g., for 1-2k token sequences on an A100-class pool you should see p95 around 200-400ms per token chunk — big caveat: tokens-per-second and batching affect that. we can run a bench for your common prompt templates.
03:33 Priya: what's the onboarding friction for our engineers? we have a lightweight marketplace team and a systems integrator team. are there SDKs and example connectors?
03:44 Claire: yes, we provide SDKs (python/node), a partner integration repo with deployment templates, and a partner onboarding checklist. Marco will share a sample connector that maps your routing policy to our policy API.
03:58 Owen: network constraints again — some customers are behind strict egress rules, we can't allow outbound to arbitrary endpoints. if we host the control plane, can traffic flow through an express route or do we need to use private link?
04:12 Marco: for private connectivity we support VPC peering, PrivateLink-equivalents, and customer-managed proxy tunnels. there may be additional networking work but it's standard. we'll need CIDR ranges and a contact.
04:27 Samir: we also need to know about data retention and model telemetry. customers won't let raw requests stay on third-party logs beyond 30 days in many contracts.
04:38 Tess: from success side — we can configure retention windows per account, and we offer audit logs streaming to your SIEM. default retention is 90 days but configurable; for pilot we can set 30 days.
04:54 Lena: curious about the prefix caching you mentioned — we have a lot of similar prompts, can caching and sharding reduce token cost materially?
05:06 Marco: yes, automatic prefix/KV caching can cut repeated token generation costs by 20-60% depending on hit rate. key point: cache hit rate depends on prompt variability. we can attach recommended batching params for different workloads.
05:22 Priya: on the reseller side we need a clear UI surface to show customers different performance tiers and estimated costs. is there a per-route cost estimation API?
05:33 Claire: we expose token-level cost breakdowns and per-route analytics in the console — you can pull estimates programmatically via our pricing API; we'll include a sample spreadsheet that maps request volume to cost per month.
05:47 Owen: deployment timeline — if we run a pilot with 2 regions and 2 instance classes (hosted pass-through only), how long to get a working pilot?
05:59 Claire: typically 2–3 weeks: week one onboarding + account set up + routing policy mapping, week two benchmark + pilot run, week three wrap + decisioning. we can compress to 10 business days for a high-priority partner.
06:14 Priya: sounds reasonable. what about quotas and rate limiting — our marketplace will fan out many small customers, does Redwood support per-tenant throttles?
06:27 Marco: yes, per-API-key rate limits, token quotas, and usage tiers. we also support burst allowances for spike traffic.
06:36 Priya: any gotchas with model licensing? some vendors require specific license terms for quantized or distilled variants.
06:47 Marco: good call — our catalog indicates license types per model. for some open models we provide quantized builds under compatible licenses; we will highlight any models that can't be served under certain partner reseller arrangements.
06:59 Samir: security deep question — when you run dedicated pools for a partner, what's the isolation model? VM-level vs tenant-level?
07:11 Marco: dedicated pools give GPU-level isolation with tenant network segmentation and audit trails. control plane is logically separated; for stronger isolation we can do a private deployment. we'll add a diagram in follow up.
07:25 Lena: any notes on orchestration — we have clients that want function-calling/tooling patterns. how do you handle streaming and tool calls?
07:36 Marco: we support streaming responses, structured output, and function/tool calling. streaming is over server-sent events or chunked responses in the SDK. function-calling has schema validation and opt-in safety checks.
07:53 Claire: ok let's walk through a concrete routing example — say customer A in eu-west calls through HavenMesh marketplace, you want to select lowest-latency Redwood POP, else fallback to quantized model in eu-central, else route to a lower-cost region. how do you envision mapping that?
08:11 Priya: that's our main pattern. UI shows tier selection and we translate to routing rules. ideally the mapping is declarative.
08:21 Marco: our policy API accepts declarative routes with priorities (latency, cost, region). we'll share a sample JSON policy. note that cross-region failover may incur longer tails; we suggest canary rollouts for critical customers.
08:36 Owen: do you support dynamic routing based on observed latency in near real-time?
08:44 Marco: we have metrics-driven routing: the smart router can shift traffic by policy threshold (e.g., p95 > 800ms triggers fallback). there's also manual overrides.
08:54 Priya: are there any existing partner reseller integrations we can see as reference?
09:00 Claire: yes — we recently integrated with Verdance (reference) and can share an anonymized case study. i'll include it.
09:09 Tess: quick note on support — partners typically get a joint onboarding call with our solutions engineers and an assigned partner success manager.
09:19 Priya: perfect. one more on billing — we need to surface per-tenant metering usage for downstream invoicing. can you emit metering CSVs?
09:31 Claire: yes, usage exports and per-key metering available. we can also stream events to your billing system.
09:40 Samir: we need to validate your crypto and key usage — do you support customer-provided keys for encryption at rest?
09:48 Marco: yes, we support customer KMS with envelope encryption and HSM integration for private deployments. for hosted we can broker keys but recommend private deployment for strict KMS controls.
09:59 Priya: ok let's capture concrete pilot scope and owners — i can commit to a 2-week pilot for hosted pass-through routing across eu-west and us-east with two model families.
10:12 Claire: excellent. proposal: pilot goals: validate routing correctness, measure p95 latency for your typical prompts, measure cost delta with caching on/off. deliverables: benchmark report, routing policy template, and onboarding doc.
10:28 Priya: yes. timeline?
10:30 Claire: we'll aim to kick on 2025-07-07 (setup) and run 2025-07-09 to 2025-07-23 for the pilot period, with a mid-pilot sync after 1 week. that matches the action items in the notes.
10:45 Owen: final technical ask — can you provide a lightweight benchmark harness (docker) so we can run tests from our POPs? we want synthetic but also replay of real traces.
10:56 Marco: i'll assemble a bench harness (node/python) that can replay traces and collect request/response latencies and cost. will include instructions for running from POPs.
11:07 Lena: good. can we also get a sample routing policy that includes per-customer QoS and rate-limits?
11:15 Marco: yes will include.
11:18 Priya: any expected integration blockers?
11:22 Marco: the main blockers are network connectivity (VPC/PEering), model license checks for certain quantizations, and per-tenant identity mapping. none of those are show-stoppers.
11:33 Claire: sounds like consensus. recap of next steps: claire sends deck + routing sample; marco sends bench harness + policy templates; priya shares SKU & commercial motion; samir will review SOC2 + provide network contacts. we'll schedule pilot kickoff for 2025-07-07.
11:55 Priya: sounds good, thanks everyone.
12:00 Claire: thanks, we'll follow up with links.

Action items (again):
- Claire: partner integration deck + sample routing policy (due 2025-07-02)
- Marco: benchmark script + replay harness + sample traces (due 2025-07-07)
- Priya: reseller SKUs and commercial motion document (due 2025-07-03)

Recorded notes on transcription quality: medium — some technical terms mis-transcribed (K V cash for KV cache, PrivateLink transcribed as private linky at one spot). Accurate enough for action items.
